name: Phoebe (deaconess in Cenchreae)
title: Servant of the Church
summary: Phoebe was a deaconess in the church at Cenchreae, a port city near Corinth. She was entrusted by Paul to deliver the Letter to the Romans to the church in Rome and is described as a protector and benefactor of many, including Paul himself.

keyEvents.title: Paul's Recommendation
keyEvents.description: Paul recommends Phoebe to the church in Rome, calling her "our sister" and deaconess of the church at Cenchreae.

keyEvents.title: Described as a Protector
keyEvents.description: Paul describes Phoebe as a prostatis (protector/benefactor) for many, including himself, indicating that she was a woman of means and influence.

keyEvents.title: Bearer of the Letter to the Romans
keyEvents.description: Phoebe was most likely entrusted with bringing the Letter to the Romans from Corinth to Rome, an important task that shows the trust Paul had in her.
